title: Remove Duplicates from Sorted List II
statement_short: Given the head of a sorted linked list, delete all nodes that have duplicate numbers, leaving only distinct numbers from the original list. Return the linked list sorted as well.
constraints: 0 <= number of nodes <= 300, -100 <= Node.val <= 100, list is sorted in ascending order
hint: Small node count (<= 300) permits an O(n) single pass, skipping duplicate value blocks using dummy and precursor pointers.
keywords: delete all nodes that have duplicate numbers
list is sorted in ascending order
why_not: Right: Two Pointers (dummy head and lookahead pointers) bypasses all nodes matching duplicate values in O(n) time and O(1) space. Not HashMap / Hash Set: Frequency counting in a hash map identifies duplicates in O(n) time but uses O(n) extra space and requires list reconstruction. Not Stack: Pushing nodes onto a stack does not inherently filter duplicate sequences without extra frequency checks. Not Sliding Window: Sliding window techniques compute subsegment properties rather than unlinking duplicate node clusters.
